note: Discovery does not authorize repair. Each finding names the narrowly scoped follow-up it should become. Nothing here was fixed by issue #233.

findings.title: Wednesday's declared editorial role never reaches Wednesday's generation prompt
evidence: scripts/generate_and_publish.py:920-922 renders the role's rules for both surfaces into _editorial_role_rules.
scripts/generate_and_publish.py:1863-1868 appends render_sources_of_record(...) to the same variable because the Wednesday role sets require_source_transparency: true (business_strategy.json:441).
scripts/generate_and_publish.py:1878-1880: `if is_wednesday_role(_editorial_role_identity): article = generate_for_wednesday(editorial.to_legacy_dict())` — one argument.
src/never_blank/wednesday_routing.py:57 `def generate_for_wednesday(signal: dict) -> dict` accepts no role rules, no CTA mode, no strategy views, no closing contract.
The Monday/Friday branch at scripts/generate_and_publish.py:1882-1890 passes editorial_role_rules=_editorial_role_rules into generate_article().
The only Wednesday consumer of _editorial_role_rules is recompose_platform(...) at scripts/generate_and_publish.py:2151-2157, which runs only when editorial acceptance revised the article.
findings.consequence: On a normal Wednesday run the role's nine structure rules, nine prohibitions and per-surface Wix/LinkedIn rules are computed and discarded, and the article is produced from the hardcoded _SYSTEM_PROMPT constants in src/never_blank/wednesday_july/*.py alone. Editing the Wednesday role in business_strategy.json changes nothing a reader sees, except after a revision. Note the boundary precisely: the Wednesday rubric (:924) and the sources-of-record block for the reviewer and reviser (:2013-2019) DO reach acceptance. It is generation, and only generation, that the role does not reach.
findings.action: Owner decision required. Do not repair here.
findings.overlaps: Issue #237 (editorial-wiring forensic) owns the Monday/Wednesday prompt-wiring question and is blocked on an owner choice. This audit records the reachability fact and makes no product choice.
findings.follow_up: Track under #237; do not open a competing issue.

findings.title: The Wednesday product contract is declared twice; only one declaration runs
evidence: WednesdayGoldenProfile.load() (src/never_blank/wednesday_golden.py:167) has no caller in src/ or scripts/.
generation_rules() (:195) and source_eligibility_rules() (:173) likewise have no production caller.
The module is imported at runtime only as a side effect of src/never_blank/__init__.py:7, so it appears reachable to an import-graph check while none of its behaviour executes.
Its own docstring at :197-201 states the canonical entrypoint carries the declared role through the generic renderer and that this renderer 'remains useful for strict profile tests'.
Callers are tests only: tests/test_wednesday_golden.py:37-42, tests/test_no_mandatory_thesis.py:296, and tests/test_wednesday_diagnostics.py:127 which parses the YAML directly.
findings.consequence: Two files describe the Wednesday editorial contract in product language. One is enforced, one is only validated by tests. A change made in the wrong one is silently inert, and the test suite will still pass.
findings.action: Name the source of truth in both files. Either give the profile a production consumer or mark it explicitly as a test-only conformance model, the way src/publishing/release_scope.py:20-26 marks its own boundary.
findings.follow_up: New issue: 'Wednesday Golden product contract has two declarations — name the source of truth'.

findings.title: prompt_rule_references declares six documents as product rules; five are never loaded
evidence: strategy/current/business_strategy.json:306-341 declares seven prompt_rule_references.
Only 'active-campaign-strategy' is functionally consumed, and only as a version equality check: src/strategy/execution_context.py:296-315 assert_campaign_reference().
config/brand_voice.md has no reader in src/ or scripts/ at all.

config/brand.yaml is read by src/quality/voice.py:159, src/quality/rewrite.py:56 and src/internal/strategy.py:73 — all reachable only from scripts/generate.py and scripts/dry_run.py, neither of which any scheduled workflow runs.
No path under strategy/methodology/ or docs/PLATFORM_AND_VISUAL_STRATEGY.md is opened anywhere in src/ or scripts/.
The only assertion about any of them is tests/strategy/test_never_blank_business_config.py:80-86, which checks `resolved.is_file()`.
findings.consequence: The configuration states that the product's voice, editorial strategy, platform strategy and visual strategy are rules the run follows. Nothing reads them. A brand-voice change has no effect on any published article, and a green test suite says the references are fine.
findings.action: Either load the declared references into the prompt chain, or narrow prompt_rule_references to what is actually consumed and re-describe the rest as human methodology.
findings.follow_up: New issue: 'prompt_rule_references declare documents no loader reads'.

findings.title: Publishing schedule has a duplicate Friday owner, an unserialized publisher, a Sunday firing and a secret-gated daily path

sub_findings.title: Two workflows publish on Friday
evidence: .github/workflows/scheduled_publish.yml:23-24 — cron 17 8 and 17 9 on day 5 (Friday 04:17 ET); its header says 'Friday remains on this legacy path until #144'.

.github/workflows/research_generate_and_publish.yml:33 — cron '0 7 * * 5,0' (Friday and Sunday 07:00 UTC); its comment says only that Monday and Wednesday moved away, and that 'Friday and Sunday remain unchanged here'.
Both reach a publisher: scripts/scheduled_publish.py and scripts/generate_and_publish.py respectively.
sub_findings.consequence: The reasoning the repository applied to Monday in #142 — two publishers on one day is two articles — applies unaddressed to Friday.

sub_findings.title: The Friday legacy publisher is not in the shared concurrency group
evidence: monday_publish.yml:53-55, wednesday_golden.yml:32-34 and research_generate_and_publish.yml:37-39 all declare `concurrency: group: never-blank-publish`.
scheduled_publish.yml declares no concurrency block at any level.
sub_findings.consequence: Friday's legacy run is not serialized against the other publishers, which share strategy/published_content_index.jsonl and data/research/published_signal_ids.txt.

sub_findings.title: Publishing days exist outside the stated Mon/Wed/Fri cadence
evidence: research_generate_and_publish.yml:33 fires on Sunday as well as Friday.
visibility_publish.yml:6-7 fires Tuesday and Thursday.
The most recent scheduling work describes the cadence as Monday/Wednesday/Friday (commit 58afe47, '#232 Scheduling: Monday/Wednesday/Friday publish at 04:17 America/New_York').
sub_findings.consequence: Reverse reachability: live scheduled publishing on four days that the current scheduling narrative does not mention.

sub_findings.title: The daily research workflow's publish behaviour is not answerable from the repository
evidence: daily_signal_research.yml:5 runs every day; :85 runs the pipeline.
:82-83 an inline shell guard sets NB_RESEARCH_PUBLISH_ENABLED=false only when the local weekday is Wednesday.
On every other day the publish/no-publish decision is the value of the NB_RESEARCH_PUBLISH_ENABLED secret, which is not visible in the repository.
sub_findings.consequence: Whether a second article is published on Monday, Friday or any other day cannot be determined from source. #159 forensics (src/publishing/release_scope.py:12-18) record that this path did publish live, to the wrong channels, for two days in September 2026.

findings.action: Establish a single documented owner per publishing day, put every publisher in the never-blank-publish concurrency group, and make the daily path's publish authorization readable from the repository.
findings.follow_up: New issue: 'One owner per publishing day; serialize every publisher'.

findings.title: 93% of tracked files are test-generated run artifacts for two synthetic signal IDs
evidence: 7,796 of 8,399 tracked files are run artifacts under those two IDs: 1,583 run directories for sig-test-001 and 1,176 for sig-identity-test-001. Every path is enumerated in reports/repository_audit/inventory/12a_sig_test_001.paths.txt and 12b_sig_identity_test_001.paths.txt.

reports/content_packages/sig-test-001.json and sig-identity-test-001.json are the same residue in flat form, and those two did match daily_signal_research.yml:106's flat glob and were committed by the daily workflow itself.
Neither ID exists outside tests: tests/test_run_identity.py:63, tests/test_visual_contract.py:78, tests/test_wednesday_supply.py:302, tests/test_wednesday_live_fixes.py:401.

Root cause: scripts/generate_and_publish.py:320-321 — `PACKAGES_DIR = Path("reports/content_packages")` followed by `PACKAGES_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` at module import. The path is relative to the process CWD, so importing the module from a test writes into the tracked repository path.

The daily workflow's commit step (daily_signal_research.yml:106) adds `reports/content_packages/*.json` — a flat glob — so it is not the source of the nested directories; a developer `git add -A` after a local test run is.
findings.consequence: Repository integrity and reviewability: any diff, any search and any file-by-file audit is dominated by artifacts with no consumer. It also makes a real content package harder to distinguish from test residue.
findings.action: Give the artifact root an injectable base (or a tmp_path default under pytest) so tests cannot write into the tracked path, then remove the accumulated directories in a separate change.
findings.follow_up: New issue: 'Tests must not write into reports/content_packages/'. Cleanup of the 7,796 files should be a second, separate change so the mechanism fix is reviewable.

findings.title: The prompts that look like the product's article prompts are unreachable from every scheduled run

sub_findings.title: config/prompts/blog_post.yaml and linkedin_post.yaml are legacy-only
evidence: src/content/generator.py:126 and :134 are their only loaders.
generator.py is reached only from scripts/generate.py, invoked only by generate_content.yml:47 and generate_and_publish.yml:52 — both workflow_dispatch-only.

The published article and LinkedIn derivative are produced from hardcoded _SYSTEM_PROMPT constants (src/editorial/platform_composer.py:114/:511, src/editorial/never_blank_voice.py:29/:162, and the wednesday_july equivalents) plus business_strategy.json role rules.

sub_findings.title: Workflow and script names collide
evidence: .github/workflows/generate_and_publish.yml calls scripts/generate.py and scripts/publish.py (lines 52, 106-108).
scripts/generate_and_publish.py — the canonical entrypoint — is called by monday_publish.yml, wednesday_golden.yml and research_generate_and_publish.yml.
The workflow named after the canonical script is the one that does not call it.

sub_findings.title: docs/SYSTEM_MAP.md re-authorizes dead artifacts
evidence: SYSTEM_MAP.md:28 lists config/content_matrix.yaml, which no code opens.
:29 lists config/intelligence.yaml, loaded only by the unreachable scripts/dry_run.py.
:30 presents config/prompts/blog_post.yaml as 'Blog generation prompt' without qualification.
:55-58 lists the four observation/topic prompts as current; three are orphaned and one is status: not_needed.

findings.action: Correct docs/SYSTEM_MAP.md to say which path each artifact belongs to, and mark the legacy V1 prompt set as legacy in-band (the way config/prompts/image_hook.yaml uses `status: not_needed`).
findings.follow_up: New issue: 'SYSTEM_MAP describes the legacy path as current'.

findings.title: Orphaned prompts and configuration kept alive by a single unreachable script
evidence: scripts/dry_run.py:95-100 is the sole loader of the three observation/topic prompts, and :82 the sole loader of config/intelligence.yaml.
No workflow runs scripts/dry_run.py and no test imports it, so those four artifacts have no executing consumer.
config/content_matrix.yaml has no loader at all; its only mention in the repository is docs/SYSTEM_MAP.md:28.
config/intelligence.yaml:1 reads `sources: []  # populated in Phase 7 (Intelligence Engine)`.
scripts/render_card_audit.py has no workflow or test; reports/card_audit/*.png (26 files) is its output and nothing reads it.
findings.consequence: Six configuration artifacts present themselves as current (`status: ready`) while nothing can execute them. The repository already has the better pattern: config/prompts/{image_hook,topic_score,strategy_brief}.yaml carry `status: not_needed` and src/utils/config_loader.py:49-53 refuses to load them.
findings.action: Confirm with the owner, then either mark these `status: not_needed` with a reason or remove them together with scripts/dry_run.py. Do not delete on static evidence alone.
findings.follow_up: New issue: 'Retire or re-declare the dry-run-only configuration artifacts'.

findings.title: Artifacts whose purpose or reachability could not be established safely

sub_findings.title: src/investigation/hypothesis_generator.py has no production importer and a self-contradicting spec
evidence: No import of src.investigation.* exists in src/ or scripts/; the only consumer is tests/test_hypothesis_generator.py.
docs/LERA_OPERATING_SYSTEM.md:5-7 records 'Branch: feature/business-investigation-layer / Status: Under development. Not merged to main' — while both the document and the module are in main.

sub_findings.title: The documented research Stage 8 has no caller
evidence: docs/NEVER_BLANK_RESEARCH_PIPELINE.md:75 lists sync_from_sheets.py as 'Stage 8: Pull edits from Sheets'; :57 describes its allowlist behaviour as current.
scripts/research/run_daily_research.py:25-32 imports nine sibling stages; sync_from_sheets is not among them, and no workflow invokes it.
Its only repository consumer is tests/test_research_pipeline.py:14 importing ALLOWED_FIELDS.

sub_findings.title: A test double lives under src/
evidence: src/research/adapters/fake.py has no production importer; tests/test_research_artifact_lifecycle.py:31 is its consumer.

sub_findings.title: Five operator scripts and four strategy modules have compile-only coverage and no runner
evidence: scripts/strategy/{build_monthly_plan,run_weekly_review,run_monthly_review,approve_strategy_recommendation}.py are only py_compiled, at strategy_tests.yml:64-67; no workflow executes them and no test imports them.

They are the sole production consumers of src/strategy/{market_analyzer,content_planner,decision_engine,pattern_extractor}.py (build_monthly_plan.py:27-28, run_weekly_review.py:30, run_monthly_review.py:23).
approve_strategy_recommendation.py is the only path that archives a strategy after human approval (run_monthly_review.py:123).

findings.action: Record each one's status where a reader will find it: a module docstring or an in-band status marker, not a stale branch header or a pipeline document.
findings.follow_up: New issue: 'State the status of the investigation layer, Stage 8 and the strategy operator tools'.

findings.title: Tests that prove existence or shape, not consumption

sub_findings.title: tests/strategy/test_never_blank_business_config.py:80-86 asserts declared references exist on disk
sub_findings.consequence: This is the test that lets F3's five unconsumed documents pass as wired product rules. It would pass unchanged if every one of them were empty.

sub_findings.title: tests/test_research_prompts.py asserts YAML shape and phrase presence in the file
sub_findings.consequence: These prompts happen to be wired, but the test would not have noticed if they were not: it never observes a model call.

sub_findings.title: tests/test_wednesday_golden.py validates a profile production never loads
sub_findings.consequence: Substantial test weight behind config/never_blank/wednesday_golden.yaml makes F2's unwired duplicate look like the live contract.

sub_findings.title: tests/test_cross_platform_overlap_policy.py:326-333 asserts on the text of config/brand_voice.md
sub_findings.consequence: Asserting a rule's absence from a file nothing loads makes the file look governed.

findings.action: Adopt the guardrail in section 9 of the human report: for every artifact classified as authoritative product config, one test that puts a distinctive value in and finds it in the actual model message.

findings.title: Four permanently accepted test failures on the legacy generator
evidence: All four entries are tests/test_editorial_pipeline.py::TestGeneratorTelegramStories — the Telegram/Stories path of the legacy V1 generator (src/content/generator.py:158,:176).
The comparator itself is strict and fail-closed (scripts/ci/check_test_baseline.py:28-42): it rejects both new and resolved failures, so the baseline cannot silently grow.
findings.consequence: Small and well-contained, but the four failures are on a path classified LEGACY_INTENTIONAL, so they are debt on code nothing schedules.
findings.action: Resolve or delete alongside whatever decision F6a produces about the legacy V1 path.

repair_order.why: A duplicate publisher on a live day can publish a second article this week. It is the only finding with a same-week product consequence.
The Wednesday role is declared and discarded. Blocked on the #237 owner decision; ranked here so it is not lost behind cleanup work.
Brand voice and editorial strategy are declared as rules the product runs on. Every week they stay unwired is a week of articles no voice document governed.
Mechanism fix first (tests stop writing into the tracked path), cleanup second. Cheap, non-controversial, and it makes every later review readable.
Two declarations of one contract; low risk to resolve once F1 is decided, and resolving it early prevents another inert edit.
The guardrail. Put it in before the cleanup below, so nothing re-enters the repository unwired.
Documentation correction. No runtime risk, high reader risk.
Orphan retirement. Requires owner confirmation and should never be done on static evidence alone.
Status statements for the unresolved artifacts.
Resolve with whatever decision the legacy V1 path receives.
